title: Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles
summary: Random surfaces on a hard substrate often exhibit entropic repulsion, wherein the surface is propelled upwards to allow entropically preferable downward fluctuations. A particularly rich class of examples arises from the low-temperature 3D Ising model. A powerful approach to studying such surfaces is through their level curves, which form a family of non-intersecting random curves. In [CIW18, CIW19], an ensemble of Brownian lines with geometrically increasing area tilts was proposed as a putative limiting model in this case.
